transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

This symptom—stopping mid-cycle but resuming when you open and close the door—is a classic sign of an intermittent fault in the door interlock system. The microwave has safety switches that cut power if it thinks the door is opening or not fully latched; if one of these is dirty, misaligned, or failing, it can cause random stops. Before we consider internal electrical faults, let's rule out a simple mechanical obstruction. With the appliance unplugged, please check the plastic hooks on the edge of the door and the slots they click into. Is there any food grease or debris in those slots that might stop them engaging fully?
Yes, there was some grease around the door hooks and latch slots. I cleaned it off, but it has still stopped once since. No smell, sparks or tripping, by the way.

[Heading: Intermittent door interlock switch fault]
The microwave stops because a safety switch momentarily thinks the door is opening; this is usually caused by a failing microswitch or a latch mechanism that isn't holding perfectly. 1. Alignment: With the appliance unplugged, close the door firmly. Does it sit flush with the surrounding cabinetry, or does it wobble? A misaligned door can pull on the switch contacts.
2. Feel: Operate the door handle a few times. Is the action smooth and firm, or does it feel loose, stiff, or 'gritty'? This helps us distinguish between a mechanical alignment issue (which might be adjustable) and a failing electrical switch inside the casing.

The door looks very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't be sure. It's screwed into the tall unit so I can't take it out to look inside. I'll check the handle feel, but it seems to stop more when I close the door gently.

[Heading: Failing door interlock microswitch]
The fact that it stops more often when you close the door gently is a strong clue: it suggests the internal safety switch isn't making perfect contact unless the latch is pushed in firmly. This points to either a worn latch hook or an intermittent microswitch inside. Please try closing the door with a bit more firmness for your next use. If it runs reliably when you close it firmly but stops again when closed gently, the internal microswitch is likely failing (it needs replacement). If it still stops even when you snap the door shut, the latch mechanism itself may be worn or misaligned. Note: Because this involves the internal safety interlock system and mains voltage, if the switch is confirmed faulty, it requires a qualified engineer to replace safely. Please do not open the casing yourself.
Ok, I'll try closing it firmly for a while and see if it still stops. It's out of Bosch's 2-year warranty, but I'd pay for a Bosch engineer visit if it comes to that.

[Heading: Failing door interlock microswitch or worn latch hook]
As discussed, opening the casing to replace these parts involves mains voltage and high-voltage risks, so it must be done by a qualified engineer. Given your willingness to book one, I recommend contacting Bosch Service directly for a repair visit. In the meantime, try closing the door with slightly more firmness; if that prevents the stops temporarily, you can continue using it safely until the engineer attends.
